scope: separate public spot study; no inference about validated futures execution
question: does choosing a good-looking long/flat rule survive later dates, costs, slower orders and another coin?

momentum.rule: long when close exceeds the completed close n observed bars earlier; otherwise flat

mean_reversion.rule: long below prior n-close mean by entry_z sample standard deviations; exit at prior mean; warmup flat

selection.metric: development net daily account-capital Sharpe in base
selection.tie_break: lower development fill count, then configuration id
selection.later_use: keep BTC development choice fixed in both later periods and ETH; report every candidate too

execution.position: one coin unit or flat; cash-funded, no borrowing
execution.fill: observed daily bucket's first trade open at or after completed bar end plus declared delay; assumed execution, no bid/ask or exact first-trade timestamp
execution.mark: observed daily close; unliquidated final inventory retained and marked, with no invented final sale
execution.interest: idle cash earns zero; no staking, lending, funding or tax

statistics.uncertainty: paired circular block bootstrap on calendar daily P&L; descriptive, no correction for candidate selection
statistics.walk_forward: prior three calendar years select a continuously simulated candidate; inspect next year; not a switching portfolio

prior_exposure: broad crypto price history was known before this study. the 2017-2026 source coverage and maximum opens were inspected to check funded sizing. no output from this declared 14-candidate spot grid was viewed before this lock. these are historical comparisons, not a prospective untouched holdout. all published spot grid results were viewed before this identity migration.
research_questions: count positive-gross candidates that stay positive after base costs at the same delay in each split
compare the BTC development winner with median candidate and flat/always-long in later periods
show candidate ranks and whether the BTC choice transfers to ETH without reselection
measure cost-only effects at one-day delay, delay-only effects at base costs, and combined stress separately
report paired annual mean-return differences with 3/5/10-day intervals and the continuous-state walk-forward diagnostic
limitations: one BTC and one ETH have different dollar risk even with the same capital; account returns are not an equal-risk comparison
fixed positive long/flat inventory, no shorting; OHLC bars cannot validate spread or intraday fill availability
asset, window and grid choices already reflect research judgment; confidence intervals do not undo prior knowledge
revision_rule: write a new version and lock before reading strategy returns if source coverage forces a change
revision_reason: identity migration after the published spot results; no strategy changes or new untouched-data claim
